analysis:
This PR only changes scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, an offline unit test for the CI workflow. It adds helpers (lines 155-184) and assertions about CI cache and checkout behavior. It touches no provider runtime code, coordinator contract, key handling, attestation, or prefix-cache storage, so no threat-model asset or boundary (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-041 and so on) is directly affected.

The new assertions tighten CI hygiene:
- Only pushes to master/dev save caches (lines 785-810), so a PR cannot poison a cache that later runs restore.
- Checkouts use persist-credentials: false (lines 844-848), so a token is not saved into the cached .git.
- Sparse checkout excludes only evidence archives and landing videos (lines 854-881).
- Actions are pinned by SHA (lines 155-157).
- The cached checkout is the only step allowed continue-on-error, and the cold fallback fails the job (lines 812-852).
- Parity and gate steps must fail without continue-on-error.

The tests read repository files and spawn subprocesses with stub scripts in temp dirs. They run offline with no secrets. The temp directories are local, created by tempfile, and not attacker-controlled.

The tested workflow, composite action and scripts are not in the supplied evidence. I cannot confirm that the real ci.yml satisfies these assertions, and it is outside this diff. No security regression is identified from this file alone.
